## The paper

**NV-Reason-CT: 3D Visual Language Model for CT Analysis** (Myronenko, Yang, Tang, Turkbey,
Simon, Harmon, Makwana, Aboian, Azamat, Hamamci, Er, Menze, Edgar, He, Guo, Xu — NVIDIA /
NIH / collaborators, [arXiv:2609.27511](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27511)).

Code: [NVIDIA-Medtech/NV-Reason-CT](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Medtech/NV-Reason-CT).
Weights: [`nvidia/NV-Reason-CT`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NV-Reason-CT).
NVIDIA blog:
[Introducing NV-Reason-CT](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/introducing-nv-reason-ct-open-3d-ct-vlm-for-radiologist-chain-of-thought-reasoning/).

CT is volumetric — hundreds of slices, findings that only make sense across depth, laterality, and
extent. Most "3D" VLMs still flatten or aggressively pool the volume before the language model
sees it, so the LLM gets a 1D bag of visual tokens without an explicit depth–height–width grid.
NV-Reason-CT's bet is the opposite: a **native 3D ViT** (Primus / COLIPRI init) that keeps
**all** visual tokens, passes them through a projector **without** spatial token merging, and
feeds explicit 3D coordinates into the LLM via multimodal RoPE (paired with **Qwen3.5-4B**).

On top of that geometry story sits the reasoning story, extended from their earlier
[NV-Reason-CXR-3B](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23968) chest X-ray work: train the model to write
radiologist-style chain-of-thought (observations → differentials → uncertainty → answer), not
just a final label. Training is two-stage — **SFT** on a curated ~550k multimodal instruction
corpus from ~70k CT inputs (expert-narrated interpretations + report-grounded synthetic
reasoning + VQA / multi-turn / refusals), then **GRPO** with verifiable rewards over chest and
abdominal abnormality sets.

Headline numbers from the paper (as published, not re-run here): on CT-RATE, macro-F1 **0.614**
and macro-AUROC **0.871** *without* a task-specific classification head; report-derived
macro-F1 **0.592**. A preliminary radiologist study reported favorable confidence and about
**50%** lower average interpretation/reporting time when assisted by the model.

## Explaining in easy words

Imagine a doctor flipping through a thick flip-book of body slices. A hollow spot only becomes
"a nodule in the upper left lung" when they remember where they are in the book (top vs bottom,
left vs right) and how many pages the spot spans. Most AI systems glance at a few pages, mash
them into a short summary sticky-note, and ask a language model to write the report from that
sticky-note. NV-Reason-CT instead keeps a sticky-note for *every* little cube of the volume,
labels each sticky-note with its page/row/column, and makes the language model reason while
those location labels are still attached. Separately, it practices thinking out loud the way a
radiologist does — "I see X, that could be A or B, I'm less sure about C" — and gets rewarded
when the final call matches verifiable abnormality checklists.

## Explaining for a data scientist

Two design choices matter more than the marketing:

1. **Dense 3D tokens into the LLM, with coordinates.** The vision tower emits a $24 \times 24
   \times 24$ grid (~13.8k tokens). No attention pooling / Perceiver-style compression before
   the language model. Explicit depth/height/width indices ride along via MRoPE so
   left-vs-right and craniocaudal extent are first-class during joint vision–text attention —
   not only inside the ViT. That is a deliberate contrast with CT-CHAT / Merlin / COLIPRI-CRM
   style connectors that flatten or pool away the grid.

2. **Reasoning as supervised product + RL on verifiable findings.** Expert-narrated CT reads
   (scarce) seed both direct SFT targets and a rewriting pipeline that turns source reports into
   synthetic narrated interpretations *constrained by the report*. GRPO then optimizes
   region-specific abnormality and report-structure rewards — so you can RL without needing an
   expert CoT for every volume. The paper is explicit that a fluent rationale is *not* proof of
   faithful internal computation; the CoT is treated as a reviewable clinical explanation
   alongside the image and final answer.

The older sibling NV-Reason-CXR did the SFT→GRPO recipe on 2D chest X-ray with Qwen2.5-VL-3B;
CT is the volumetric generalization, not a different philosophy.

## Jargon-buster

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| **Native 3D ViT** | A vision transformer that treats the CT as a volume of patches with 3-axis position, not a stack of independent 2D images. Think of reading the flip-book as one 3D object instead of unrelated photos. |
| **Spatial token merging / pooling** | Compressing thousands of visual tokens into a short sequence before the LLM. Saves compute; throws away fine spatial layout the LLM never sees. |
| **MRoPE (multimodal rotary positional encoding)** | Rotary position encodings that can index vision tokens with depth/height/width (and text with sequence position) in the same attention stack. |
| **COLIPRI / Primus** | NVIDIA's prior CT representation work; NV-Reason-CT initializes its 3D encoder from those weights, then trains end-to-end (encoder not permanently frozen). |
| **GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)** | An RL algorithm (DeepSeek-R1 family) that scores several sampled answers relative to each other. Here the rewards are verifiable abnormality / report-structure checks. |
| **Verifiable reward** | A scorer you can compute automatically (e.g. does the answer match the abnormality label set?) so RL doesn't need a human preference judge every step. |
| **Report-grounded synthetic reasoning** | LLM-rewritten "radiologist thinking" text constrained by the real report — scales CoT supervision without inventing clinical facts not in the source. |

## Architecture — traced from the paper

Pipeline, in order:

- **Input.** Regional chest or abdominal CT volume (not a random 2D slice salad).
- **3D vision encoder.** Primus ViT with three-axis RoPE, initialized from COLIPRI; emits
  dense volumetric patch tokens ($24^3$).
- **Projector.** Learned map into the LLM embedding space — **keeps every token**, no extra
  spatial merge.
- **Language model.** Qwen3.5-4B; visual tokens enter with explicit 3D coordinates via MRoPE.
- **Outputs.** Structured reasoning + answers: abnormality Q&A, report generation, multi-turn
  follow-up, with observations / differentials / uncertainty made explicit for human review.
- **Training stage 1 — SFT.** End-to-end on ~550k instruction examples (~70k unique CT inputs):
  reports, finding- and anatomy-focused Qs, multi-turn, refusals, expert + synthetic narrations.
- **Training stage 2 — GRPO.** Region-specific verifiable rewards on chest/abdomen abnormality
  sets and report structure.

## What I'm taking / skipping for defect-inspection VLMs

Personal shortlist — mapped to GDXray / casting void work and the agentic defect series, not to
"deploy this CT model on the line."

**Will try (ideas, not the CT checkpoint):**

- **Verifiable-reward GRPO after reasoning SFT.** For multi-label defect vocabularies, a CoT
  that ends in a checkable abnormality / defect set is a cleaner RL target than vague
  preference scores. Same shape as "measure reject rate on generative edits" discipline —
  reward what you can verify.
- **Expert traces as seeds, report/label-grounded synthetic CoT as scale.** I will never have
  550k radiologist narrations for voids; I might have a handful of inspector think-alouds plus
  lots of bbox/mask labels. The paper's split — scarce expert demos guide rewriting, source
  labels constrain content — is the transferable data recipe.
- **Make spatial indices first-class when the modality is volumetric.** If I ever go micro-CT
  / multi-view rather than single 2D radiograph, "don't pool away the grid before the LLM"
  is the architectural warning label to remember.
- **Treat CoT as an audit artifact, not proof of internals.** Useful for human review and
  error analysis (their radiologist study angle); dangerous if I market it as "the model
  showed its work faithfully."

**Will not test:**

- **Dropping `nvidia/NV-Reason-CT` onto GDXray castings.** Wrong modality (3D clinical CT vs
  2D industrial X-ray), wrong ontology (chest/abdomen findings vs porosity), and the useful
  part is the training recipe, not the checkpoint.
- **Replicating the full 550k / two-region medical corpus pipeline.** Out of scope for a
  semiconductor defect blog post; also not the bottleneck I have (I lack inspector CoT and
  rare-defect volume, not another CT-RATE).
- **Assuming fluent reasoning ⇒ calibrated uncertainty.** Paper already hedges this; I should
  too.

**If time allows:**

- **Side-by-side with NV-Reason-CXR-3B on 2D radiographs** as a closer relative to industrial
  X-ray than the CT model — still medical, still OOD for castings, but the 2D reasoning stack
  is the fairer "does CoT+GRPO help classification?" probe.
- **Tiny GRPO toy on a verifiable defect checklist** (e.g. presence of ≥1 bbox-overlapping
  prediction) after a short SFT CoT stage on local Qwen-VL — measure whether verifiable RL
  moves checklist F1 or just makes longer prose.

## The honest bottom line

NV-Reason-CT is not a model to fine-tune for void detection. It is a clear, open recipe for
**keeping 3D structure all the way into the LLM** and for **training reviewable radiologist-style
reasoning with SFT → verifiable GRPO**. For my line of work, the geometry lesson applies only
when the input is truly volumetric; the reasoning+RL lesson applies now, on 2D X-ray VLMs,
if I'm willing to build a small expert-seeded CoT set and a checklist reward I actually trust.

Next concrete step when this draft graduates: either a CXR-3B smoke test on a public chest
film (closer modality) or a minimal verifiable-GRPO toy on GDXray — not a CT reimplementation.
